content.title: What Happens When Oil and Gas Wells Die? West Virginia Has a New Plan for That
content.summary: West Virginia is expected to unveil on Thursday a potentially first-of-its-kind fund aimed at one of the thorniest environmental issues plaguing America’s oil-and-gas-producing regions.  Diversified Energy  one of America’s largest owners of natural-gas wells, said it would plow $70 million into the fund over the next 20 years in the hope that those holdings grow to as much as $650 million through compounding interest and returns.  The goal is to continue capping and plugging old oil and gas wells even if Diversified goes out of business.
